title: I Posted the Chicken-Coop Nest Hours After They Camped My Numbered Boxes

parts.text: I stepped into the coop at 6:02 a.m. and chair Len was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE BOX. TWENTY MINUTES. NESTS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-three, garden secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered boxes. Len shrugged. "Chairs are the coop." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover straw on my numbered boxes. Then I asked for the nest log. At 6:10 the shed pinged why Len's name was on my straw. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shed can see Len's leftover straw on my numbered boxes.

social.video_title: They camped my numbered nest boxes on my hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Chicken coop, leftover straw, a twenty-minute clock he posted. I logged the nests. Would you have asked for the nest log?

parts.text: Len called it collect until the shed asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the straw still. The boxes went back to my numbered slot. Len ran a slot of his own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE COOP. I keep my boxes on a labeled shelf. Len brown-bags his collect. The coop finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Nest log, numbered boxes, and a second line on the board. Was collect ever my straw?
